clue.text: Prepare to shoot early rouser

blocks.note: first meaning: to raise the hammer of a gun ready to fire
second meaning: the farmyard bird that crows at dawn

explanation.surface: A hunter gets ready to fire at the crack of dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a sportsman up early; the second half is really the bird that wakes everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: You cock a gun's hammer before firing, and a cockerel crowing at daybreak wakes the household.

clue.text: Competent, father cutting wire

indicators.note: something cutting into a line sits inside it, so one word is placed within the other

blocks.note: a cable is a thick wire
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A handy dad snipping through a wire like a skilled electrician.
explanation.definitionFit: Capable and competent are synonyms, both meaning able to do something well.

clue.text: Grass (cannabis) at start of orgy for telly addict

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: couch grass is a common weed grass
pot is slang for cannabis
taken as written
the first letter of orgy

explanation.surface: Drugs and an orgy sound like a wild night, which is rather livelier than a night in front of the box.
explanation.walkthrough: Telly is British slang for television; the answer is someone who spends hours slumped watching it.
explanation.definitionFit: A couch potato is an idiomatic term for a lazy person who watches a great deal of television.

clue.text: Deny any connection with pig breaking racket

indicators.note: something breaking into a noise bursts into the middle of it, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: a din is a loud racket
a sow is a female pig

explanation.surface: Someone disclaims all responsibility for a noisy pig that has burst into a scene.
explanation.definitionFit: To disown someone is to refuse to acknowledge any relationship with them.

clue.text: Fellow holding paper monster

indicators.note: someone holding something has it in their grasp, so one word wraps around the other

blocks.note: a don is a university fellow
rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper

explanation.surface: A man clutching a newspaper with a frightful creature on the front page.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragon is a fire-breathing beast of legend, a classic mythical monster.

clue.text: Collection of music for bongos? Possibly yes

indicators.note: possibly hints that the word could be something else, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the drums, used as letters
OK signals agreement, like yes

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a book of sheet music would suit a bongo player and seems to get a yes.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram takes the drums and the agreement together, all eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A songbook is a volume gathering many songs, that is a collection of music.

clue.text: Quip made by learned chap

blocks.note: surface reading: a witty remark from an academic
setter's reading: a joke from a wise person would be a wise one, and a joke is also called a crack

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer in two: a learned person is wise, and a crack is a joke, so his joke is literally a wise one.
explanation.definitionFit: A wisecrack is a smart or flippant remark, a quip by another name.

clue.text: Capital invested in Laos? Lots

indicators.note: money invested in something is put inside it, so the letters sit within the following words

blocks.note: runs across the end of one word and start of the next

explanation.surface: A financier wonders whether money has gone into Laos and is told plenty has.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital meant is a city, not money; Laos is a distraction as a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital city of Norway, so it is an example of a capital.

clue.text: Former German state? American in Paris confused

indicators.note: in places one word within the letters of the other
confused letters are muddled up, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: the city, used as letters
US is short for American

explanation.surface: Echoing the film An American in Paris, a muddled tourist asks about old German history.
explanation.definitionFit: Prussia was a kingdom and later a state of Germany, abolished after the Second World War.

clue.text: Cosy place in Vine Street

indicators.note: in tells you the letters lie within the words that follow

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A snug home found on Vine Street, a London street on the Monopoly board.
explanation.definitionFit: A nest is a bird's home and, figuratively, any snug and comfortable retreat.

clue.text: Extremities of Sark, the ancient island

indicators.note: the extremities of a word are its two ends, its first and last letters

blocks.note: the first and last letters of Sark
ye is an old spelling of the

explanation.surface: The far ends of one Channel island and an old island of legend.
explanation.walkthrough: Sark is one of the Channel Islands, a nice decoy for an island answer. Ye in shop names like Ye Olde Tea Shoppe is an archaic form of the.
explanation.definitionFit: Skye is a large island of the Inner Hebrides off the west coast of Scotland.

clue.text: Novel about New York choirboy I suppressed, using any means

indicators.note: a suppressed thing is kept out, so that letter is dropped from the word before
new suggests a fresh form, so the letters that follow are rearranged
about means surrounding, so the first word goes around the rest

blocks.note: a novel is a book
the city, used as letters
taken as written
the letter to be dropped from the choirboy

explanation.surface: A story about a New York chorister in which the narrator keeps quiet about himself.
explanation.walkthrough: New York looks like one place, but New is the signal acting on York plus the choirboy minus his I; the novel then wraps around the result, split one letter in.
explanation.definitionFit: By hook or by crook is an idiom for achieving something by whatever method it takes, fair or foul.

clue.text: Finished film, past one's prime

blocks.note: something over is finished
The Hill is a 1965 Sean Connery war film

explanation.surface: A completed movie, with a jibe that its star is getting old.
explanation.definitionFit: Over the hill is an idiom for someone too old to be at their best.

clue.text: Girl in the Spanish/French river

blocks.note: el is Spanish for the
the Oise is a river in northern France

explanation.surface: A young woman paddling in a river on the Franco-Spanish border.
explanation.walkthrough: The slash makes it look like one river shared by two countries; it really separates two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Eloise is a female first name, so a girl's name as crosswords often use.

clue.text: First to see head attack fall guy

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of see
a cape or headland is a promontory
to go at someone is to attack them

explanation.surface: Someone is told to watch the man who leads the assault and then takes the blame.
explanation.walkthrough: Head is a geographical headland here, not a leader or a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: A scapegoat is a person made to take the blame for others, which is what a fall guy is.

clue.text: Take notice of damaged boat entering English river

indicators.note: damaged things are knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
something entering goes inside, so one part is placed within the other

blocks.note: the Nene flows through Northamptonshire into the Wash
taken as written

explanation.surface: A warning to pay attention to a wrecked boat drifting into a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Nota bene is Latin for note well, an instruction to the reader to pay attention.

clue.text: Envoy's certificate and original of testimonial

indicators.note: the original of a word is where it begins, its first letter

blocks.note: a diploma is a certificate of qualification
the opening letter of testimonial

explanation.surface: An ambassador's credentials: a certificate and a reference.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe s is read as is, joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A diplomat is an official representing a country abroad, and an envoy is one such representative.

clue.text: Liqueur, one taken by a girl after end of cabaret

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept
after places what comes before it later in the answer than what follows it

blocks.note: the last letter of cabaret
the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl at a cabaret show ordering a drink when it is over.
explanation.walkthrough: One taken by a: I is followed by A, then the girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Tia Maria is a brand of coffee-flavoured liqueur from Jamaica.

clue.text: Fuss excessively when entertaining duke

indicators.note: a host entertaining a guest has them inside, so one part goes within the other

blocks.note: too means excessively
D is an abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: Someone goes over the top when hosting an aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: A to-do is a commotion or palaver, an informal word for a fuss.

clue.text: Small sailing boat in rough drawing

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a ketch is a two-masted sailing vessel

explanation.surface: A little yacht depicted in a quick pencil drawing.
explanation.walkthrough: Small sailing boat reads as one phrase, but small only gives its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A sketch is a quick, unfinished drawing that outlines a subject.

clue.text: Chopper's door, extremely efficient

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the word, its first and last letters

blocks.note: a hatch is a small door or opening
the first and last letters of efficient

explanation.surface: Praise for a helicopter's door, which works extremely well.
explanation.walkthrough: Chopper suggests a helicopter but means a cutting tool; the apostrophe s reads as is.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatchet is a small axe, a tool used for chopping wood.

clue.text: Approach a meeting place

blocks.note: taken as written
a venue is where an event or meeting is held

explanation.surface: Someone heading towards the spot chosen for a gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: An avenue can mean a way of approaching a problem, or a tree-lined approach to a house.

clue.text: Make all possible efforts to get Lorna's flat to the highest standard?

blocks.note: Lorna Doone is the heroine of R. D. Blackmore's novel
flat ground is level
the best is the highest standard

explanation.surface: Bringing Lorna's apartment up to scratch, as estate agents might promise.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is re-split: Lorna's surname with a possessive becomes do one's, and her flat is not a home but level ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To do one's level best is an idiom for trying as hard as one possibly can.

clue.text: Blowing top, smack yobbo

indicators.note: losing its top means the word's first letter is removed

blocks.note: a clout is a heavy blow

explanation.surface: Losing one's temper and hitting a hooligan.
explanation.walkthrough: Blowing top looks like losing one's temper; here it removes the first letter. Yobbo is British slang for a rowdy, uncouth young man.
explanation.definitionFit: A lout is an aggressive, ill-mannered man, the same as a yobbo.

clue.text: Acceptable conduct in class

blocks.note: first meaning: proper behaviour
second meaning: a year group or class at a British school

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about behaving in a lesson; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is bad form means it breaks etiquette, and in British schools a form is a class of pupils.

clue.text: Feed ours around one in New Hampshire

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are moved about into a new order
in places the jumbled letters inside the abbreviation that follows

blocks.note: the US state's postal abbreviation
taken as written
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A request to feed our own family members while we are away in New Hampshire.
explanation.definitionFit: To nourish is to provide with food needed for growth and health, so to feed.

clue.text: Nation securing superior sculpture

indicators.note: something securing another holds it fast inside, so one part wraps the other

blocks.note: a state is a nation
U means upper class, a British label for superior usage

explanation.surface: A country commissioning a grand monument.
explanation.walkthrough: U as in U and non-U was a 1950s British label for upper-class speech and habits.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue is a carved or cast figure, which is a kind of sculpture.

clue.text: Gunpowder, for one, left in container

indicators.note: in places one letter inside the word that follows

blocks.note: a pot is a container
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Explosive powder stored with what remains in a tin.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gunpowder Plot was the failed 1605 scheme to blow up the English Parliament, remembered on Bonfire Night.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gunpowder Plot is a famous example of a conspiracy or scheme, which is a plot.
